blocks.text: The selected Vladimir-Suzdal museum photograph identifies a twelfth-century panel. Mary stands at full length with a scroll, turned toward Christ in the upper corner; extensive historic surface loss remains visible.

blocks.text: The published tradition distinguishes the icon transported by Andrew, later known as the Vladimir icon, from the new image commissioned to record the vision. The OCA places the journey in 1155 and gives June 18 for the Bogolyubov commemoration. The age and location of this selected museum panel are supplied by its own artwork record.

blocks.text: The OCA’s account describes Mary lifting her hand toward Christ and receiving His blessing. It also records later variants with groups of saints. Those details belong to the source’s account of the type; this worn historic example is not silently identified with every later Moscow variant.
